questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
Which statement is the most valid reason for government intervention in a free market economy?

options.A: Consumers are well informed, making it difficult for producers to make profits.
options.B: Health and education are not available in sufficient quantities.
options.C: Producers are motivated by profit maximisation.
options.D: There are many competitive firms and not enough sole suppliers.

R Q P S good Y T O S T PR Q good X The working hours of the labour force are reduced by law. Which curve could be the country’s new production possibility curve?

questions.questionText: The provision of which service by governments could be explained by the concept of public goods?

options.B: health services
options.C: law enforcement
options.D: public libraries

questions.questionText: Which change does not have an immediate effect on the position of the demand curve for a product?

options.A: a fall in the price of a complementary product
options.B: a range of new products entering the market
options.C: a rise in the labour costs of its production
options.D: an increase in the price of a substitute product

questions.questionText: What is correct about market supply?

options.A: Market supply can increase only when all individual firms increase their output.
options.B: Market supply is effective when consumers have sufficient income to buy the good.
options.C: Market supply is the result of aggregating the supply of all individual firms.
options.D: Market supply of an inferior good falls as price increases.

questions.questionText: In which circumstances must the total expenditure by consumers on a good increase when its price increases?

options.A: if demand for the good is income-elastic
options.B: if demand for the good is price-inelastic
options.C: if the price of a complementary good also increases
options.D: if the price of substitute goods also increases

questions.questionText: The price elasticity of demand for good X is 1. At a price of $12, quantity demanded is 4000 units. What will be the price when the quantity demanded is 20000 units?

The cross-elasticity of demand of good S with respect to the price of good P is +1.5. The cross-elasticity of demand of good S with respect to the price of good R is –1.5. The cross-elasticity of demand of good P with respect to the price of good R is –1.5. What can be concluded about goods P, R and S?

options.A: S and P are complements; P and R are substitutes.
options.B: S and P are complements; R is an inferior good.
options.C: S and P are substitutes; P and R are complements.
options.D: S and P are substitutes; R is an inferior good.

questions.questionText: A manufacturer’s ability to increase supply in the short run will be greater

options.B: if spare capacity exists.
options.C: if the product is perishable.
options.D: if unemployment is low.

questions.questionText: In 2009 the Chinese government faced decreased demand in export markets and wished to increase the sales of electrical goods made in China. Which policy would have achieved this aim?

options.B: increasing the restrictions on the manufacture of electrical goods
options.C: removing a tariff on imported products
options.D: subsidising the sales of electrical goods in China’s poorer rural areas

questions.questionText: Which is a transfer payment?

options.B: payments of rent
options.C: unemployment benefit
options.D: wages of government employees

What must be true if an economy is experiencing inflation?

options.B: Aggregate supply is decreasing.
options.C: The interest rate is increasing.
options.D: The real value of money is decreasing.

questions.questionText: Suppose the average consumer’s expenditure is divided between bread, meat, milk and vegetables in the ratio 4:3:2:1. During the course of a year, the price of bread falls by 10%, the price of meat increases by 20% and the prices of both milk and vegetables increase by 10%. What is the increase in the average price level during the year?

In August 2013, a Dutch insurer announced it wished to sell its South Korean Life Insurance group to a South Korean company for $1.65 billion. How would such a sale be recorded on the Dutch balance of payments?

options.A: a negative entry in the direct investment section of the financial account
options.B: a negative entry in the investment income section of the current account
options.C: a positive entry in the direct investment section of the financial account
options.D: a positive entry in the investment income section of the current account

Why might a government decide to increase the quota set on imports?

options.A: to cut a deficit on the trade balance in goods and services
options.B: to encourage diversification in home industry
options.C: to lower domestic unemployment
options.D: to raise the level of international trade

questions.questionText: What can be considered an expansionary supply-side policy?

options.A: an increase in government expenditure on training
options.B: an increase in sales tax
options.C: an increase in the rate of interest
options.D: an increase (revaluation) of the exchange rate

questions.questionText: In an attempt to correct a balance of trade deficit, the government of Indonesia has decided to employ expenditure-dampening methods. Which policy would best fit this description?

options.B: raising income tax rates
options.C: subsidising home-produced goods
options.D: taxing imported goods
